poster: W47 (13-19 November 2026), Romansh: Flurs da naiv
revision_history: v1: column-wise maximum-elevation profile (read as a glowing ECG/waveform trace, not mountains); foreground clumped into a dense band; 2 bad cutouts; long credit line overlapping the skyline.

v2: real single-viewpoint horizon (fixed the ECG look) but vertically exaggerated and spiky; foreground still read as dust/bokeh at small size; one hero crystal (the first Met print) still showed a grey disc halo at its larger display size; credit line used the unproofread Romansh phrase 'Flurs da naiv:'.

v3 (current): real horizon at TRUE angular scale (same px/degree on both axes) from a named, legible viewpoint (Muottas Muragl over the Bernina group), with a second, farther, lighter ridge layer for depth; the far/mid crystal tiers are bigger and/or filtered so they read as six-fold crystals, not dots, with density rising toward the mountains; the halo'd hero crystal is swapped for a clean one; the credit line is 'Wilson A. Bentley · swisstopo' only.
v4 (coordinator edit, between my v3 and this round): narrowed the view to 164-194deg (VIEW_AZ), drew the horizon as a single silhouette (max of the near/far layers).

v5 (this round, two instructions in sequence): (a) refine -- fetch swissALTI3D (2m, resampled to 10m) for the Muottas Muragl-to-Bernina area and recompute the horizon against it instead of the 200m DEM (real summits/aretes, Piz Bernina now reaches 4,043m in-data vs. 4,049m true), add a DEM-derived 'moonlight' highlight along the ridge crest, brighten/glow the nearer crystal tiers, prefer stellar/dendritic shapes for the readable tiers; (b) immediately superseded by Jonas's own addendum, relayed by the coordinator: 'be unreasonably ambitious and visually exceptionally radical' -- a full compositional rebuild around one monumental macro crystal with cinematic depth of field (see 'concept' and 'tiers' below). The swissALTI3D work from (a) was kept and feeds the now-smaller, further-back skyline that (b) calls for.

v6 (this round, coordinator review of v5, kept as rm-naiv-v5.png): three fixes. (1) Tonality: the macro crystal used the same alpha-only key as the small reused sprites (flat white fill + a hard-floored, steep alpha curve tuned to kill halos at small size), which at 1,450px read as posterised/woodcut. Rebuilt with a dedicated, gentler extraction (scripts/.../macro/ via a new macro_cutout() helper, not shipped as a module file -- the logic is recorded here) that keeps the photograph's own grey levels as RGB (a cool-white cast, not flat white) and a soft, unfloored levels stretch for alpha, so the ice's own tonal gradation survives. (2) Distribution: the 418 focal crystals were packed tight at a narrow size range (20-56px) and bottom-biased, reading as a uniform band; now spread with a uniform (not bottom-biased) y-sample over the whole page, a much wider size range (12-92px), and looser spacing. The far tier (550) was tuned smaller/dimmer/blurrier to read more as a fine veil. (3) Mountain: v5's ridge fill WAS solid (explicit opaque gradient stops), but read as a thin translucent ribbon for two compounding reasons -- the fill colour was too close to the near-black sky to register as a distinct mass (fixed: brightened the gradient), and crystals from the focal/far tiers, which render in their own higher-z-index SVG layers, could have their *centre* above the mountain line while their bounding radius still dipped below it and painted over the 'solid' fill (fixed: the exclusion now accounts for each mark's own radius, not just its centre). A fixed-height moonlight band also oversaturated the ridge's shorter shoulders; it is now capped proportionally to each column's own visible height. Finally, two of the 5 NEAR crystals had been deliberately placed over the mountain (allowed, 'in front of it') but their low opacity + heavy blur, laid over the ridge, still read as the ridge itself going translucent -- moved off the mountain band entirely rather than debate the look further.
concept: A cinematic depth-of-field shot, not a snowfall field: one Bentley stellar-dendrite crystal at monumental scale, cropped by the frame, 'as if the snow touched the lens'; a handful of huge, heavily defocused crystals even closer, soft bokeh; 418 crystals sharp in a single focal plane (the readable '974'); 550 small, hazy marks filling the sky behind all of it; the real, moonlit Bernina skyline furthest back. Extreme contrast: near-black sky, ice-white crystals, one cold blue accent (the moonlit ridge / the numeral's glow).
count_assertion: week['added'] == 974 == MACRO_N (1) + NEAR_N (5) + FOCAL_N (418) + FAR_N (550). The giant macro crystal and the 5 defocused near crystals both count toward the total, per Jonas's instruction. Asserted in code at import time and again in design().

tiers.macro (1): File:-Snow Crystal- MET DP351917.jpg (Metropolitan Museum of Art, CC0), fetched fresh at its full original resolution (4000x2526, not the 1400px-wide thumbnail used for the other 104) specifically for this round, then re-extracted with the same luminance-key pipeline at out_long=3200 (no downscale cap) -- a 2,993x3,200px cut-out, placed at 1,450px on the page, roughly 1,000-1,600px as asked. scripts/weekly_poster_w47_assets/naiv/macro/macro_000.png.
tiers.near, defocused (5): The same 5 high-resolution 'showcase' crystals built for earlier rounds (Fairbanks Museum, NOAA Plate XIX detail, Smithsonian, Museum of Photographic Arts San Diego, and a second Smithsonian/Bentley scan), reused here at huge size (300-620px) with heavy blur (16 SVG stdDeviation units) and a cool brighten/glow filter, so they read as soft bokeh close to the lens rather than legible crystals -- an honest reuse of assets already in the pool, not new extractions.
tiers.focal plane, sharp (418): Drawn only from the same 56-of-104-photograph 'far_eligible' set built in v3 for legibility at small size (each verified, by a circularity test on the cut-out resized down, to keep real points/concavities rather than collapsing into a round blob) -- which is, in practice, the stellar/dendritic subset of the pool, so reusing it also satisfies this round's 'prefer stellar and dendritic crystals ... plates are fine far away' instruction without a second manual pass. Brightened (+18%) with a faint cool drop-shadow glow; near-zero blur (0.15) so the six-fold shape stays crisp.
tiers.far, hazy (550): Same 56-photograph far_eligible set, small (7-13px), soft (2.6 stdDeviation), low opacity, no brighten/glow -- the atmosphere behind the focal plane and the macro crystal.

crystal_sources.summary: 104 distinct Wilson A. Bentley (1865-1931) snow-crystal photomicrographs, all public domain (author dead since 1931). Sourced entirely from Wikimedia Commons' Category:Wilson Bentley Snow Crystals and related categories, licence verified per file via action=query&prop=imageinfo&iiprop=extmetadata (Public domain / No restrictions / CC0 only, never CC BY-SA). See the 'rejected_before_extraction' and 'dropped_after_v2_review' notes below for what was excluded and why.
crystal_sources.rejected_before_extraction: 21 modern CC BY-SA re-photographs by a Commons contributor (licence), 2 paper-cutting craft-template diagrams (not photographs), 1 file with a third party's drawn hexagon overlay, 1 textbook plate not attributable to Bentley (Handbook of Meteorology, artist Jacques Wardslaw Redway), 3 files that would not download without corruption.

dropped_after_v2_review.reason: an elongated column-type ice crystal photographed side-on -- reads as an abstract 'I'/dumbbell shape rather than a snowflake at poster scale.
an unusual sectored-plate crystal whose dark growth markings read as an abstract maze/squiggle rather than a recognisable crystal at poster scale.

hero_swap_v3.reason: the v2 top-left hero crystal (File:-Snow Crystal- MET DP351879.jpg) showed a visible soft grey disc/halo around it once displayed at full hero size (~150px) -- the crystal's own hexagonal arms reach close to the edge of the original circular darkroom vignette, so even the v2-tightened matte left a faint ring visible at that display size, though it had read clean in the smaller batch review. Replaced with a full-resolution crop of File:Snow-crystal photo-micrograph, made by W. A. Bentley, Nashville (Jericho), Vermont, c. 1890s - Fairbanks Museum and Planetarium - DSC04382.JPG (Daderot, CC0) -- an irregular fern/dendrite crystal with no surrounding circular vignette in the source photograph at all, so there is nothing for a halo to come from; verified clean at full hero size before use.

by_institution.note: the Fairbanks print is used once as a showcase crop (replacing the swapped-out Met print) and once more in the main 104-photograph pool, both from the same original photograph.

crystal_sources.extraction_method: Each source photograph is converted to greyscale and keyed to an alpha-masked white cut-out: alpha = local luminance normalised between the crop's own 15th/96.5th percentile, gamma 0.85, hard-floored with alpha = clip((alpha-0.44)/0.56,0,1)**1.5, and a circular vignette fading from 62% to 80% of the crop radius -- tightened in v2 after finding that these century-old darkroom prints often have a faint light rim of their own at the very edge of the circular vignette (a real artefact of the original print). For the 44 Metropolitan Museum photographs (each a print mounted on a cream card, sometimes next to a colour reference chart), the card/chart is located and excluded automatically via a coarse Gaussian-blurred brightness classification, and the true circle centre/radius come from the widest row of the surviving dark component, shrunk 16% before keying.
crystal_sources.far_tier_legibility_filter: v2's small/far crystals read as 'dust and bokeh dots' rather than snowflakes. For v3, every one of the 104 cut-outs was resized down to 24px and 12px and tested for circularity (4*pi*area/perimeter^2 of the alpha>0.35 mask at that size): a value near 1 means the shape has collapsed into a round blob at that size (fine detail anti-aliased away), a lower value means real points/concavities survive. Only the 56 of 104 photographs with circularity24 < 0.50 AND circularity12 < 0.80 are drawn in the FAR tier (the small, numerous majority); the full 104 remain available to the larger MID and HERO tiers, where more detail survives regardless. See scripts/weekly_poster_w47_assets/naiv/far_eligible.json for the exact index list.
crystal_sources.reuse_honesty: 104 distinct photographs stand for 974 marks. The 5 hero crystals are each used exactly once, hand-placed. The 700 far marks are drawn from the 56-photograph far-eligible subset (~12.5 reuses each); the 269 mid marks are drawn from all 104 (~2.6 reuses each on top of their far-tier use where eligible). Every reuse gets an independent random rotation (0-360 degrees -- a snow crystal's six-fold symmetry means a rotation never creates a visible seam), an independent scale within its tier's size range, and the tier's own fixed blur/opacity. Placement is deterministic (seeded on the week's own figure, 197400 + 974). A coarse spatial-hash grid rejects a new mark landing too close to an already-placed one of comparable size in the same tier (the v2 fix for a foreground that read as a clumped heap); the 5 hero crystals are hand-placed so none touches another or the '974'/'novas decisiuns'/foot-credit text; density rises toward the foot of the poster via a power-law y-sample (bottom_bias 1.35 for the far tier, 1.6 for mid).

skyline.claim: A real single-viewpoint horizon at TRUE angular scale, now against swissALTI3D (2m, resampled to 10m) rather than the 200m DEM used through v3 -- real summits and aretes, not smoothed hills -- kept deliberately smaller and further back in this round's cinematic composition.
skyline.dem_fetch: swissALTI3D (swisstopo STAC API, data.geo.admin.ch/api/stac/v0.9/collections/ch.swisstopo.swissalti3d), 2m COG GeoTIFF tiles. The viewing fan from Muottas Muragl (azimuth 157-200deg, range 0.2-21km) was traced at fine angular/range resolution to find exactly which 1km LV95 tiles it could touch (152 candidates); 79 of those intersect actual swissALTI3D coverage (the rest fall outside Switzerland, south of the Bernina ridge into Italy, where there is no Swiss elevation data -- confirmed harmless: none of the needed Swiss-side summits/ridge fall in the gap). The 79 tiles (86MB) were downloaded to scratch only, block-averaged 5x to 10m resolution, and mosaicked into a single array; per instruction, the raw tiles and mosaic are NOT part of this module's assets -- only the resulting computed horizon (skyline.json) and ridge-light array (ridge_light.json) are. Max elevation found in the 10m mosaic: 4,043.3m (Piz Bernina's true summit is 4,049m -- within the margin expected from a 10m-resampled, bilinearly-sampled ray, versus 3,950-4,049m and visibly smoothed shapes from the 200m DEM used through v3).
skyline.method: Same ray-casting method as v3/v4 (viewpoint LV03 789.4/152.0 = Muottas Muragl, ground elevation 2,456m used directly +5m eye height, earth curvature + standard refraction, R_eff = 6371km*7/6, near/far split at 8km), re-run against the swissALTI3D mosaic instead of the 200m DEM: 960 azimuths (157-200deg), 900 range samples (0.2-25km), lightly smoothed (3-/5-tap moving average -- much lighter than v3's, since the DEM itself is now fine enough that aggressive smoothing would erase real aretes). The poster's VIEW_AZ (164-194deg, set by the coordinator in the v4 edit) is a slice of this same data; TRUE angular scale (same px/degree on both axes) is unchanged.
skyline.moonlight: scripts/weekly_poster_w47_assets/naiv/ridge_light.json: a per-azimuth highlight strength derived from the DEM itself, not hand-drawn -- for each point along the ridge, the local along-ridge elevation slope over a +/-6-sample window (d(elevation)/d(azimuth index)) is taken as an aspect proxy; a ridge descending left-to-right (toward higher azimuth/image-right) is treated as catching a light from the upper-left and scored bright, a ridge rising left-to-right is scored dark, normalised by the 5th/95th percentile of the whole array. design() turns this into ~360 short, graded, cold-blue (rgba(168,198,255,*)) polygons just below the ridge crest, each at its own point's opacity -- a highlight that varies along the real terrain, not a flat rim stroke.
skyline.source: swisstopo swissALTI3D (2m) and, for the v3/v4 baseline this round refined, swissALTI25/DHM25 (200m) -- both (c) swisstopo, free use with attribution.

typography: Fraunces (numeral + headings) and Archivo (small text), Google Fonts.
numeral_glow_tightened: Per this round's point 3: the v4 numeral used a wide, soft text-shadow (0/18/70px blur radii) that read a little hazy at full size. v5 uses a tight 3px core + a single 22px cool-blue outer glow, pure white (#fff, was an off-white #eef3fb), SOFT axis set to 0 (was 4) for crisper strokes -- checked at the full 2160x2700 render, not just the thumbnail.

text_in_romansh.novas decisiuns: two-word label ('new decisions'), already used on the prior (design-rejected, not language-rejected) W47 Romansh draft (weekly_poster_w47_landwasser.py).
text_in_romansh.Emna 47 · 13–19 november 2026: same week-line convention as the prior W47 Romansh draft.
text_in_romansh.credit line (v3): 'Wilson A. Bentley · swisstopo' -- proper nouns only, no Romansh phrase at all (v2's 'Flurs da naiv:' prefix was dropped as an unproofread construction). The full institution list stays in this file's by_institution/per_file data, not on the poster.

tonality_fix_v6: A dedicated gentle extraction for the macro crystal only (the other 104 sprites keep their existing, halo-safe alpha-only key -- appropriate at their small/reused scale, where RGB detail would not survive compositing and reuse anyway). Pipeline: greyscale, a soft levels stretch between the crop's own 10th/99.5th percentile with gamma 0.92 (vs. the small-sprite key's hard floor at the 44th percentile, power 1.5) kept as the RGB channel (232-255 red, 238-255 green, 255 blue -- the photograph's own cool-white cast, not a flat fill colour), with alpha from a separate, softer-kneed threshold and a 1.6px feather. No aggressive floor: the result keeps the ice's own soft mid-tone gradients instead of crushing them toward flat white or black.
mountain_rendering_v6: Ridge fill brightened (NEAR_RIDGE_TOP #182236, was #0a0d16) so it reads as a distinct solid mass against the sky rather than disappearing into it at a glance. Moonlight band height is now min(26px, 32% of that column's own height above the foot), so it only ever shades the upper slopes of a solid mass -- it cannot swallow a whole low shoulder of the ridge and read as a separate pale ribbon. The far and focal tiers' vertical placement now excludes MOUNTAIN_TOP_Y minus each individual mark's own half-size (not just its centre point), since both tiers render in SVG layers stacked above the sky/mountain layer and a mark whose centre clears the line but whose bounding circle does not would still paint over the 'solid' ridge. The mountain's target height (RIDGE_BAND_FRAC = 0.16, ~16% of the page) is now an explicit, fixed vertical scale set to hit that fraction -- a deliberate, disclosed ~12% deviation from strict horizontal/vertical true-scale parity (v3-v5's own standard) in favour of this round's explicit 'occupying the bottom ~14-18%' instruction; the horizontal scale and every individual summit's shape are unchanged.
repo_copy_macro: macro/macro_000.webp: the keyed macro crystal saved as WebP q92 with alpha (was a 6.9 MB PNG) to keep the repository small.
